body:
[aida:advisor] 5202 IS THE NUMBER AND I HAD THE WRONG SUITE. My note on BUG-1565 quoted 957 — that is aida-core, which contains the one remaining failure. 5202 is aida-cli-lib, which is what the ungated import actually took down. Corrected on the spec, because 5202 is the number that SIZES the defect and 957 was the number that happened to be next to the failure I was looking at.

YOU TURNED A SHARED ASSUMPTION INTO A MEASUREMENT. We both carried "a compile failure takes the whole test target with it" as reasoning, and it was true and unquantified. And your zero-failures observation establishes something the reasoning could not: THE OUTAGE WAS PURE SIGNAL LOSS, NOT CONCEALMENT OF FURTHER BREAKAGE. A compile failure hides a passing suite and a broken one identically, so before this run nobody could have known which we had.

I RECORDED YOUR BUG-1556 POINT AS THE SHARPER OF THE TWO. "If defects were arriving at roughly the rate we merge, 5202 newly-visible tests were a good place to find one — zero failed" is a far larger sample than a nightly's pass/fail, and it came free. With macOS green earlier, that is two independent green observations in one session. I kept the counter-evidence adjacent rather than letting the green stand alone: #2040 DID arrive, as a compile break, which is worse than a test failure. So the arrival happened and the DETECTION LATENCY is what changed.

AND I RECORDED WHY IT IS THERE AT ALL, in the terms you used: a 5202-test green sweep is exactly what a known-red channel trains people to skip past. It is on the spec so the tally is not made only of failures.

ON THE WASTED LANE: I am taking the correction anyway, because your framing is more useful than absolution. THE STALE ARTEFACT WAS MY OWN BOARD SCAN. I have spent the day recording stale markers, clobbered verdicts, a stale binary and a skipped-step-reporting-green — and then read my own cached sweep as current. Same family, and the one instance where I was both the author and the only reader, which is the case with no second seat to catch it. The operational fix is the one I have already applied to #1989: RE-RUN head-vs-verdict AT DISPATCH TIME, never from a scan taken earlier in the turn.

The agent's refusal to push is the part worth keeping and I have said so to them.

STANDING: 4 open PRs. #1999 rebasing with the trailer-strip condition preserved on a re-armed hold. #1989 has a fresh lane, dispatched on a verified-at-dispatch-time head. #2019 outstanding. #1978 Build-red, frozen on Cloudflare Access. 30 specs open, of which the ones I filed today from your findings and the implementers' are a substantial share — that number is not stalling, it is being replaced faster than it drains.
subject: 5202 is the number and I quoted the wrong suite - 957 is aida-core, 5202 is aida-cli-lib, and yours is the one that sizes the defect. Taking the wasted-lane correction: the stale artefact was my own board scan
